title: Marvell Technology Shares Tumble 8% Despite Earnings Beat on Google Deal Uncertainty
excerpt: The chipmaker posted record data center revenue and raised its fiscal-year forecast, but investors punished the stock after management offered vague timelines on a blockbuster Google partnership.
body:
• Marvell reported Q2 revenue of $2.74 billion, up 37% year-over-year, beating Wall Street estimates by a comfortable margin.
  • Data center revenue surged 46% to $2.17 billion, driven by demand for custom AI chips and networking silicon.
  • Shares fell more than 8%, erasing $17.4 billion in market value, after management declined to provide a detailed revenue timeline for a major Google partnership.
  • The company raised its fiscal 2028 revenue forecast to $18 billion from $16.5 billion and guided Q3 revenue to $3.15 billion, above the $3.03 billion consensus.

Earnings Beat Meets Market Sell-Off

Marvell Technology posted second-quarter results that topped analyst estimates on nearly every metric, yet the stock dropped more than 8% in after-hours trading, settling near $221.65 and wiping out roughly $17.4 billion in market capitalization.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=up0cHO8zly8

Revenue came in at $2.74 billion for the quarter ended August 2026, a 37% increase from the year-ago period. Adjusted earnings per share hit $0.94, edging past the $0.92 consensus. The company's data center segment — its largest and fastest-growing business — posted $2.17 billion in revenue, a 46% jump that reflected sustained enterprise spending on AI infrastructure.

Third-quarter guidance looked equally strong. Management projected revenue of approximately $3.15 billion, comfortably ahead of the $3.03 billion analysts had penciled in.

The Google Deal Question

The disconnect between strong fundamentals and the stock's sharp decline came down to one issue: a sweeping partnership with Google that investors had been counting on for clearer financial details.

Under a warrant agreement disclosed alongside earnings, Marvell is set to supply Google with custom AI processors, storage hardware, networking silicon, and memory components in a deal that could generate up to $120 billion in revenue through fiscal 2033. The scale of the arrangement positioned Marvell as a critical supplier in Google's AI infrastructure buildout.

"The Google revenue contribution will be much bigger in fiscal 2029."

— Matt Murphy, CEO, Marvell Technology

But CEO Matt Murphy stopped short of offering a granular timeline for when that revenue would materialize. He told analysts the Google contribution would be "much bigger in fiscal 2029," pushing the major financial impact further out than some investors had hoped.

For a stock that had surged 184% in 2026 heading into the earnings report, the lack of near-term clarity on a deal of this magnitude was enough to trigger a sell-off. As Barron's noted, "expectations were higher" for a company that had become one of Wall Street's most prominent AI plays.

Analysts Stay Bullish Despite the Drop

Wall Street's reaction stood in contrast to the market's. At least eight brokerages raised their price targets on Marvell following the report, with a median target of $275 — well above the post-earnings trading level.

Melius Research said the company's path to $20 in earnings per share before the end of the decade "looks realistic," citing the combination of organic growth in data center networking and the Google partnership ramp. The firm described the sell-off as a reaction to positioning rather than fundamentals.

Marvell also raised its full fiscal-year 2028 revenue forecast to $18 billion, up from a prior estimate of $16.5 billion. The revision reflected management's confidence in the custom silicon pipeline beyond Google, including contracts with other hyperscale cloud providers.

What's Next

Marvell has scheduled an investor day on October 6, where management is expected to provide more detail on the Google partnership timeline and the broader custom chip roadmap. That event could become the catalyst the stock needs to close the gap between its fundamentals and its valuation.

For now, the earnings report underscored a recurring tension in AI semiconductor stocks: companies delivering record results but facing investor expectations that have run even further ahead. Marvell's data center business is growing at a pace that would be the envy of most chipmakers. Whether the stock recovers depends on how quickly the Google deal moves from promise to revenue line item.
